mainTopic: מעילה on חלב of קדשים but not on blood, and the rule that nothing has מעילה after its מצוה is done
overview: The amud opens at the end of a משנה comparing חלב (forbidden fat) and דם (blood). חלב of a קרבן carries מעילה, פיגול, נותר and טמא, but blood applies to more kinds of creatures. The גמרא asks how we know the חלב of a שלמים carries מעילה. רבי ינאי learns it from a reverse היקש to the פר כהן משיח. When רבי חנינא asks why רבי's source "כל חלב לה׳" is not enough, אביי shows that each פסוק adds something: one brings in the kidneys and יותרת, the other brings in the sheep's אליה. This raises the question of why the אליה is not forbidden to eat, and the גמרא settles on רב זביד's answer: forbidden חלב is only fat found in ox, sheep and goat alike. Next the גמרא gives three sources that blood has no מעילה. רבי יוחנן's source rests on the rule that nothing has מעילה once its מצוה is done. The גמרא defends that rule against the case of תרומת הדשן by calling it one of "two verses that come as one". When that answer is questioned according to the view that such pairs do teach, the reply begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Stringencies of forbidden fat over blood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes listing what makes חלב stricter than דם. With a קרבן, חלב carries מעילה, פיגול, נותר and טמא, and blood does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: With forbidden fat of a sacrifice, one is liable for misusing holy property, and one is liable for eating it as פיגול, as נותר, or while impure. None of this applies to blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is in the middle of a list of ways חלב is stricter than blood, and here it gives the last items on that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the חלב comes from a קרבן, eating it can break several extra sacrificial laws on top of the plain איסור חלב. Blood of a קרבן is different. One who drinks it is liable only for the איסור דם itself, not for these sacrificial laws.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מעילה, meaning wrongful personal use of holy property
A קרבן ruined by a wrong intention about time during the עבודה, which may not be eaten
Meat of a קרבן left past its eating deadline
Eating קדשים while one is ritually impure
Which is not the case with

phrases.english: One is liable for misuse of consecrated property with it,
phrases.notes: "It" means חלב from a קרבן. The משנה is listing how חלב is stricter than blood.

phrases.english: and one is liable for it because of piggul
and notar and eating while impure,
which is not so with blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ, וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל וְנוֹתָר וְטָמֵא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חלב of a קרבן carries liability for מעילה, פיגול, נותר and טמא, and blood does not.

steps.title: The stringency of blood over forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה now turns to blood's stringency. The איסור דם applies to every kind of animal and bird, kosher or not. The איסור חלב applies only to a kosher domesticated animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood is stricter in one way. The blood prohibition covers domesticated animals, wild animals and birds, both non-kosher and kosher. Forbidden fat applies only to a kosher domesticated animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the comparison and shows the one area where blood is stricter than חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the point is how widely each איסור applies. The איסור דם covers בהמה, חיה and עוף, and covers טמאים too. The איסור חלב applies only to a בהמה טהורה, so the חלב of a deer or a bird is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency, the stricter side
A domesticated animal, such as a cow, sheep or goat
An undomesticated (wild) animal, such as a deer
A bird
Applies to, is in effect

steps.whatToRemember: Each איסור has its own stringency. חלב brings in the sacrificial laws. דם covers far more kinds of creatures.

phrases.english: And the stringency in blood
is that blood applies to domesticated animals, wild animals, and birds,
whether non-kosher or kosher,
but forbidden fat does not apply
except to a kosher domesticated animal alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the comparison from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The איסור דם applies to all animals and birds, kosher or not, while the איסור חלב applies only to a kosher בהמה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that forbidden fat carries misuse liability?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's ruling that one is liable for מעילה on חלב of a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule comes from, and this question sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is aimed at the first item in step 1, מעילה. The reason this needs a source is that the חלב in question can come from a קרבן of lower holiness, such as שלמים, and it is not obvious that מעילה applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? This is a standard request for a source.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: This is asking about the משנה's rule that eating חלב of a קרבן makes one liable for מעילה.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the חלב of a קרבן is subject to מעילה

steps.title: רבי ינאי brings a verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי points to the פסוק about the פר כהן משיח, which says its parts are removed "as from the שור of the שלמים."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: The verse says, "As it is taken off from the bull of the peace offering."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי answers the question by quoting the פסוק that will serve as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is in the section about the פר כהן משיח, the bull brought by the כהן גדול for an accidental sin. At first glance it seems only to tell us which parts of that bull are burned on the מזבח, by comparing it to a שלמים. How it actually proves מעילה comes in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Is taken off, separated (the parts set aside for the מזבח)
The peace offering, a קרבן of lesser holiness

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
As the verse says:
"As it is taken off from the bull of the peace offering,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:10. The verse is talking about the bull of the כהן משיח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק "כאשר יורם משור זבח השלמים" (ויקרא 4:10).

steps.title: What would the comparison add?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי asks: what do we really learn about the פר כהן משיח from the שלמים? Everything needed is already written about it explicitly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, then, do we learn from the bull of the peace offering?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a rhetorical question that sets up the real point. If the comparison teaches nothing new about the פר כהן משיח, it must be there to teach something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses right before this one already list all the parts of the פר כהן משיח that are burned. So comparing it to the שלמים seems to add nothing about that bull. The question pushes us to read the comparison in the other direction.

keyTerms.meaning: But really? This word introduces a rhetorical question.
Then, now (in light of what is already written)

phrases.english: But what do we learn
phrases.notes: He means learning something about the פר כהן משיח, whose parts are already listed in ויקרא 4:8-9.

phrases.english: from the bull of the peace offering, then?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה לָמַדְנוּ מִשּׁוֹר זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the verse in step 4 is actually teaching
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What purpose the comparison to the שלמים serves, since the פר כהן משיח needs nothing from it

steps.title: The comparison actually teaches about the peace offering
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is turned around. The שלמים learns from the פר כהן משיח, so just as that bull is subject to מעילה, so is the שלמים (its חלב).
steps.simpleTranslation: This verse seems to come to teach, but it turns out to learn. It compares the bull of the peace offering to the bull of the anointed priest. Just as the bull of the anointed priest is subject to misuse liability, so too the bull of the peace offering is subject to misuse liability.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי finishes the proof. The שלמים is the one doing the learning here, and what it learns is מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פר כהן משיח is קדשי קדשים, so it is clearly subject to מעילה. The שלמים is קדשים קלים, so מעילה would not be obvious. By the היקש, the parts of the שלמים that go on the מזבח, including its חלב, take on מעילה from the פר. That is the source for the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes to teach but turns out to be the one learning. This describes a comparison that works in the reverse direction.
Compares the two cases through a היקש, a comparison set up by the verse
The bull brought by the anointed כהן גדול for an accidental sin
Liability for wrongful use of holy property

steps.whatToRemember: The source that the חלב of a שלמים carries מעילה is a reverse היקש. The שלמים learns מעילה from the פר כהן משיח.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the verse the simple way, as teaching about the פר כהן משיח. Here the direction is flipped: the שלמים is the case being taught.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even קדשים קלים, which belong to their owner, have מעילה on the parts that go on the מזבח.

phrases.english: This comes to teach,
and it turns out to learn,

phrases.aramaic: מַקִּישׁ שׁוֹר זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים לְפַר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ:
phrases.english: it compares the bull of the peace offering to the bull of the anointed priest:

phrases.aramaic: מָה פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: just as the bull of the anointed priest is subject to misuse liability,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שׁוֹר זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה.
phrases.english: so too the bull of the peace offering is subject to misuse liability.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד, וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rhetorical question of step 5 by reversing the direction of the comparison
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Through a היקש to the פר כהן משיח, the שלמים (and its חלב) is subject to מעילה. This is the source for the משנה's ruling.

steps.title: רבי חנינא asks why a new source is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא challenges רבי ינאי: רבי already taught a source from "כל חלב לה׳" that the אימורים of קדשים קלים are subject to מעילה. Why look for another one?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said to him: Is what רבי taught so unattractive? He taught that "All the fat is to ה׳" includes the altar parts of קדשים קלים in מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא pushes back on רבי ינאי's derivation from the פר כהן משיח. He points out that רבי already gave a source for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that חלב of a שלמים is subject to מעילה already had a source: "כל חלב לה׳" includes the אימורים of קדשים קלים. So רבי ינאי's whole derivation looks unnecessary. The question is about why we need two sources, not about whether the rule is true.

keyTerms.meaning: Ugly, unattractive; here: is that source not good enough?
The parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
Offerings of lesser holiness, such as שלמים

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said to him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to רבי ינאי, whose derivation we just saw.

phrases.english: Is this one that Rebbi taught ugly?
phrases.notes: He means: what's wrong with רבי's source, that you need a new one?

phrases.english: "All the fat is to ה׳"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:16

phrases.english: – to include the altar parts of offerings of lesser holiness in מעילה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבי ינאי's derivation, which was just completed in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's derivation from the פר כהן משיח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An existing source ("כל חלב לה׳") already teaches the same rule, so the new derivation seems unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: "All the fat" alone would leave out the kidneys
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that both sources are needed. With only "חלב", we would include the fat but not the יותרת and the two kidneys, so the Torah adds "כאשר יורם".
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It was needed. If the Torah had written only "fat," I would have said: fat, yes; the יותרת and the two kidneys, no. So the Torah wrote "as it is removed."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי ינאי by showing that each source teaches something the other does not. This is the first half of his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "חלב" sounds like it covers only actual fat. The יותרת and kidneys are also burned on the מזבח but are not fat. "כאשר יורם" compares to everything removed from the bull, so it brings them in.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed; both sources are necessary
I would have thought (the mistaken assumption)
The יותרת, a part near the liver burned on the מזבח
Kidneys
"As it is removed": the פסוק comparing the פר כהן משיח to the שלמים

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבי's source is wrong. He is saying each פסוק covers a gap the other one leaves open.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It was necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written only "fat,"
I would have said: fat – yes,
the יותרת and the two kidneys – no.
So the Merciful One wrote "as it is removed."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:10, the פסוק רבי ינאי used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חנינא's challenge by showing why רבי ינאי's source is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only "חלב", only real fat would be subject to מעילה, not the יותרת and kidneys.
steps.terutzMaskana: "כאשר יורם" brings in all the parts removed from the bull, including the יותרת and kidneys.

steps.title: אביי: "As it is removed" alone would leave out the tail
steps.stepSummary: The second half of אביי's answer: with only "כאשר יורם", we would leave out the sheep's אליה, which a bull does not have. So "כל חלב" is needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah had written only "as it is removed," I would have said: the fat of the tail, which a bull does not have, no. So the Torah wrote "all the fat."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his answer by showing that רבי's source is needed too. Now both sources are justified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "כאשר יורם" compares to the bull, so it would cover only parts a bull has. A sheep's אליה is burned on the מזבח, but a bull has no such part. "כל חלב" covers every fat, so it brings in the אליה.

keyTerms.meaning: The fatty tail of a sheep, burned on the מזבח
It does not exist; it is not found

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources, two jobs: "כאשר יורם" brings in the יותרת and kidneys; "כל חלב" brings in the sheep's אליה.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only "as it is removed,"
I would have said: the fat of the tail,
which is not found in a bull – no,
so the Merciful One wrote "all the fat."
phrases.notes: The אליה counts as "חלב" because the Torah calls it that (ויקרא 3:9).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of אביי's צריכותא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only "כאשר יורם", the sheep's אליה, which a bull lacks, would not be subject to מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: "כל חלב" includes the אליה, so both sources are needed.

steps.title: If the tail is called fat, it should be forbidden to eat
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי challenges: if the אליה is called "חלב", it should fall under the איסור חלב and be forbidden to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said to רב זביד: If the tail is called "fat," let it be forbidden to eat!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge comes from אביי's answer. Since the אליה counts as "חלב" for מעילה, it seems it should also count for the איסור of eating חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word "חלב" is used for the איסור of eating forbidden fat. If the Torah calls the אליה "חלב", why isn't eating it forbidden? Yet in practice the אליה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is called
Let it be forbidden
Eating

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרִי לְרַב זְבִיד:
phrases.english: Rav Mari said to Rav Zevid:
If the tail is called "fat,"
let it be forbidden for eating!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 9's claim that the אליה is called "חלב" and pushes it into the איסור of eating.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the אליה is "חלב"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the אליה is "חלב" for מעילה, it should also be forbidden חלב for eating, but it is not.

steps.title: Forbidden fat is only fat found in ox, sheep and goat alike
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers from the פסוק "כל חלב שור וכשב ועז": forbidden חלב is only fat found in all three animals. The אליה is found only in a sheep, so it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About your question, the פסוק says "all fat of ox, sheep, and goat": something that is the same in ox, sheep, and goat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד answers רב מרי by reading the eating פסוק closely. That פסוק limits forbidden fat to fat that all three animals share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור of eating חלב names all three animals together. So only fat that all three share is forbidden. The אליה is only in a sheep, so even though it is called חלב for the מזבח, it is not forbidden to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that is equal or shared
Ox, sheep, and goat

steps.whatToRemember: The אליה is "חלב" for the מזבח and for מעילה, but it is not forbidden חלב for eating, because that איסור covers only fat all three animals share.
steps.confusionAlert: The same word "חלב" works differently in two places: for קרבנות it includes the אליה, but for the איסור of eating it does not.

phrases.english: He said to him: About you the verse says:
"All fat of ox, sheep, and goat"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:23

phrases.english: – something that is the same in ox, sheep, and goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מרי's challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of a פסוק that limits the איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the אליה is called חלב, it should be forbidden to eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forbidden חלב must be found in ox, sheep and goat alike; the אליה, found only in a sheep, is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical reason a sheep's אליה is permitted to eat, even though it is offered on the מזבח like חלב.

steps.title: רב אשי: the tail is only called 'fat' with an extra word
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer to רב מרי's question. The פסוק calls it "its fat, the tail", not plain "fat", so it is not included in the איסור חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is called "its fat, the tail." It is not called plain "fat."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second answer to the question of why the אליה is not forbidden to eat as חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד answered from the פסוק about ox, sheep and goat. רב אשי answers from the wording instead. The Torah never calls the tail just "חלב". It always adds the word "האליה", so it is not true חלב for the איסור of eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Its fat, the tail: the Torah's wording for the sheep's tail (ויקרא 3:9)
Plain, without any extra word

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is called "its fat, the tail,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:9

phrases.english: but it is not called plain "fat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to רב מרי's question, alongside רב זביד's answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording-based answer: the extra word shows it is not plain חלב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the אליה is called חלב, it should be forbidden as חלב
steps.terutzMaskana: Because it is only called חלב with the added word "האליה", it is not forbidden חלב

steps.title: Then the tail should not have מעילה either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב אשי. If the tail is not real חלב, then the source "כל חלב לה׳" would not include it for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, people should not be liable for מעילה with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's answer by showing that it breaks the earlier source for מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 9, the tail was included in מעילה only because it counts as "חלב" in "כל חלב לה׳". If רב אשי says it is not plain חלב, that derivation falls apart. Then the tail should have no מעילה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: now that you said this, look what follows
They will be liable for מְעִילָה, misusing holy property

phrases.english: But if that is so,
people should not be liable for מעילה with it!
phrases.notes: He means the tail. Its מעילה came from calling it "חלב" in "כל חלב לה׳".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer from step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the tail is not plain חלב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it is not חלב, the source "כל חלב לה׳" cannot include the tail in מעילה

steps.title: The correct answer is Rav Zevid's
steps.stepSummary: Since רב אשי's answer fails, the גמרא concludes that רב זביד's answer is the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the answer is like רב זביד's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב אשי's answer and settles on רב זביד's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד's answer avoids the problem. The tail really is called חלב, so it has מעילה. It is still permitted to eat, because forbidden חלב must be found in ox, sheep and goat, and the tail is found only in a sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear: this is the correct answer

steps.whatToRemember: The אליה counts as חלב for מעילה, but it is permitted to eat. Forbidden חלב is only fat found in ox, sheep and goat (רב זביד).

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear that it is like Rav Zevid.
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 11: forbidden חלב is only fat found in ox, sheep and goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes after rejecting רב אשי in step 13
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב זביד's answer stands: the אליה is permitted to eat because it is found only in a sheep.

steps.title: Where do we learn that blood has no מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words "which is not so with blood" and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Which is not so with blood": where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה, which says blood has no מעילה, and asks for the source, setting up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אימורים have מעילה, but the משנה says the blood does not. This is surprising, because blood is also given to the מזבח. The גמרא wants a פסוק that explains the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is not so with blood (words of the מִשְׁנָה)
From where do we learn these words?

phrases.english: "Which is not so with blood":
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. A person who benefits from blood of a קרבן is not liable for מעילה.

phrases.english: from where do we learn this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּדָּם, מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the אליה discussion to a new line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for why blood has no מעילה

steps.title: עולא: 'to you' means the blood is yours
steps.stepSummary: עולא learns from the word "לכם" in the פסוק about blood that it belongs to you, so it is not holy property.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The verse says "to you," meaning it shall be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the first source for why blood has no מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "I have given it to you upon the altar." עולא reads "to you" as "it is yours". If the blood counts as yours and not as Temple property, there is no מעילה on it.

keyTerms.meaning: To you
It shall be yours

phrases.english: Ulla said:
For the verse says "to you,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:11

phrases.english: meaning it shall be yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "לכם" shows the blood is yours, so it is not holy property for מעילה

steps.title: School of רבי ישמעאל: given for atonement, not for מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from "לכפר" that blood was given only for כפרה, not to have מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "To atone" means: I gave it for atonement, and not for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source for why blood has no מעילה, from the next word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the stress is on the purpose of the blood. The Torah gave it for one job, כפרה. That job does not turn it into holy property that carries מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: To atone
Atonement

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"To atone":
I gave it for atonement,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate source after עולא's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "לכפר" limits the blood to atonement and excludes מעילה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'it is' makes before atonement like after atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the word "הוא" that blood has the same status before and after כפרה. After כפרה there is no מעילה, so before כפרה there is none either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The verse says "it is." Before atonement it is the same as after atonement. Just as after atonement there is no מעילה, so too before atonement there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third source, from the word "הוא" in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הוא" means the blood stays as it is and its status does not change. After the blood is sprinkled, there is clearly no מעילה, because its job is done. So רבי יוחנן says that before sprinkling there is no מעילה either.

keyTerms.meaning: It is: it stays the same
Before atonement: before the blood is sprinkled
After atonement: after the blood is sprinkled

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said,
The verse says: "it is,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:11: "כי הדם הוא בנפש יכפר".

phrases.english: it is the same before atonement as after atonement:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: just as after atonement there is no מעילה with it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לִפְנֵי כַּפָּרָה אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third source, after עולא and the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "הוא" equates before and after כפרה, so the lack of מעילה after carries back to before

steps.title: Why not compare the other way around?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe "הוא" means after כפרה is like before. Then there would be מעילה both before and after.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: after atonement it is the same as before atonement. Just as before atonement there is מעילה, so too after atonement there is מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן by flipping his comparison around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הוא" only tells us that both stages are the same. It does not say which stage sets the rule. Maybe the normal rule before sprinkling, which is that holy things have מעילה, should carry over to after sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead: offering another reading
There is מְעִילָה with it

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא הוּא לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה כְּלִפְנֵי כַּפָּרָה:
phrases.english: But say instead: after atonement it is the same as before atonement:

phrases.english: just as before atonement there is מעילה with it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה – יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה!
phrases.english: so too after atonement there is מעילה with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא הוּא לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה כְּלִפְנֵי כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the direction of רבי יוחנן's comparison
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An equation works both ways. Why make before like after, and not after like before?

steps.title: Once an item's מצוה is done, there is no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a general rule: nothing still has מעילה after its מצוה is done. So the comparison can only go in רבי יוחנן's direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no item whose מצוה has already been done that people are still liable for מעילה with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן with a fixed rule that settles which way the comparison goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The status after כפרה is already known for certain: once the blood is sprinkled, its מצוה is done, so there is no מעילה. That stage cannot change, so it must be the model. The stage before כפרה follows it.

keyTerms.meaning: Its מִצְוָה has been done

steps.whatToRemember: Blood of a קרבן has no מעילה. There are three sources: "לכם" (עולא), "לכפר" (school of רבי ישמעאל), and "הוא" (רבי יוחנן). רבי יוחנן's source rests on the rule that once an item's מצוה is done, there is no מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule "אין לך דבר שנעשה מצותו ומועלין בו" is a general principle of מעילה that applies far beyond blood.

phrases.english: There is no item whose מצוה has been done
and people are still liable for מעילה with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה מִצְוָתוֹ וּמוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general principle that fixes the direction of the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe after כפרה should be like before, with מעילה
steps.terutzMaskana: After כפרה can never have מעילה, so before כפרה must follow it and have no מעילה

steps.title: The ashes have מעילה even after their מצוה is done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule from step 20 using תרומת הדשן, which has מעילה even after its מצוה is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that nothing has מעילה after its מצוה is done? What about תרומת הדשן? Its מצוה is already done, and yet there is מעילה with it, because the פסוק says 'and he shall put it beside the מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule it just used, that nothing has מעילה once its מצוה is done. It brings a case that seems to break that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תרומת הדשן, the כהן takes ashes from the מזבח and puts them beside it. That is the whole מצוה, yet the ashes must stay there and you may not use them. So here is something with מעילה after its מצוה is done, and that seems to knock out the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily removal of a scoop of ashes from the מזבח, placed beside it
There is מעילה with it, meaning you may not use it for yourself
But look at this case, used to bring a counterexample

phrases.english: And is there no such case?
phrases.notes: He means: is it really true that nothing has מעילה after its מצוה is done?

phrases.english: But there is the removal of the ashes,
whose מצוה has been done, and yet there is misuse with it,
as it is written: "And he shall put it beside the altar"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general rule used as the answer in step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that nothing has מעילה after its מצוה is done
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: תרומת הדשן has מעילה after its מצוה is completed

steps.title: The ashes and the כהן גדול's clothes are a special pair that teaches nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are two verses that come as one, so they do not teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and the כהן גדול's clothes are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach for other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule. It says תרומת הדשן is an exception, not a model for other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two places where the Torah gives מעילה after the מצוה is done: the ashes and the white clothes of the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים. When the Torah says the same new rule in two places, that tells us the rule stays with those two cases only. So the general rule still holds everywhere else, including blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses that teach the same thing; the rule stays limited to those cases
They do not teach (a rule for other cases)
The priestly clothes; here the white clothes of the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think two verses would make the rule stronger. Here it is the opposite: if the Torah needed to say it twice, it shows the rule does not spread to other cases.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵאי תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וּבִגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה
phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes and the priestly vestments are
(two verses that come as one),

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵאי תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וּבִגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21

steps.terutzMaskana: תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are a limited pair, so the general rule stands

steps.title: According to רבי דוסא, the clothes are not part of the pair
steps.stepSummary: The answer only works for the רבנן, who say the clothes must be put away. According to רבי דוסא they can still be used, so the ashes are left alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the רבנן, who say 'and he shall leave them there' teaches that the clothes must be put away. But for רבי דוסא, who says it only means the כהן גדול may not use them on another יום הכפורים, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 22. It shows the pair does not work for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the clothes must be put away for good, so there is מעילה after their מצוה, and they make a pair with the ashes. According to רבי דוסא, the clothes are only banned for the כהן גדול on a later יום הכפורים, so they are not a case of מעילה after the מצוה. Then the ashes stand alone, and one case alone could teach a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one opinion)
Putting holy items away, so no one uses them
What is there to say? (the answer does not work here)

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בגדי כהונה pair with תרומת הדשן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי דוסא the clothes do not need גניזה, so they are not a case of מעילה after the מצוה, and the ashes are left as a single case

steps.title: The ashes pair with עגלה ערופה instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new partner for the ashes: עגלה ערופה. Together they are two verses that come as one, so they do not teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach for other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the clothes and gives the ashes a different partner, עגלה ערופה. This works for everyone, including רבי דוסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עגלה ערופה is treated here as another case that stays forbidden after its מצוה is done. So the ashes are still part of a pair, and the pair does not teach a general rule. The rule from step 20 stands, and so does רבי יוחנן's reading that blood has no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered person is found and the killer is unknown
Rather; drops the earlier answer and gives a new one

steps.whatToRemember: There is no מעילה after a thing's מצוה is done. The ashes are an exception, but because they pair with עגלה ערופה as 'two verses that come as one', they teach nothing for other cases, like blood. This holds for the view that such pairs do not teach. The next step challenges it from the other view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the general rule that step 20 used to back רבי יוחנן's reading of 'הוא' about blood.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because the removal of the ashes
and the heifer whose neck is broken
are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵאי תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by replacing the partner case from step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the paired case so the rule of שני כתובים הבאין כאחד works for all opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי דוסא, the ashes stand alone and could teach a general rule
steps.terutzMaskana: The ashes pair with עגלה ערופה, so they do not teach, and the general rule stands

steps.title: The answer only works for one opinion about paired verses
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 24 depends on the view that two verses that come as one do not teach a general rule. According to the view that they do teach, what can we say?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says that two verses that come as one do not teach. But for the one who says they do teach, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the answer from step 24. It says that answer only works according to one side of a known disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement about two verses that teach the same thing. One opinion says they don't teach a general rule, because the Torah would not need two verses if the rule were general. The other opinion says they do teach a general rule. According to that second opinion, תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה would together teach that things keep their מעילה after their מצוה is done, and the rule from step 20 falls apart again.

keyTerms.meaning: They do teach, meaning the law spreads to other cases as a general rule

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is rejecting the 'two verses' idea. It accepts it. It is only pointing out that the answer from step 24 doesn't satisfy the opinion that such verses DO teach.

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says they do not teach
phrases.notes: 'They' means two verses that come as one, like the ashes and the עגלה ערופה from step 24.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says they do teach
what is there to say?

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 24 that תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are two verses that come as one and so do not teach a general rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That answer assumes paired verses don't teach. According to the view that they do teach, the two cases would teach a general rule that מעילה stays after the מצוה is done. That would contradict the rule from step 20.
